plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample gene-level count matrix (counts.csv) from Salmon with a matching metadata.csv (one row per sample, condition column): 6 atopic-dermatitis lesional skin samples vs 6 controls, unpaired, single batch, human. The research question asks which genes and which hallmark pathways change, and flags that one sample (sample_01) has a library size about 4x below the median. All scripts are Python, per the user constraint — pydeseq2 (0.5.4) and gseapy (1.3.1) are both installed, so no R is needed.

The flow is: (T1S1) sample-structure QC on the raw counts — library sizes, detected genes, blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap — with sample_01 kept and inspected rather than dropped, because DESeq2 size factors already account for depth and removal at n=6 per group would cost real power; drop it only with a stated reason, and if it is dropped run the DE both ways and report both. (T1S2) pydeseq2 Wald test of condition (lesional vs control, control as explicit reference denominator) on the counts as delivered — the profile does not state whether the Salmon gene-level counts carry a length correction, and there are no quant.sf files or average transcript-length table in the inputs, so no length offset can be applied and this limitation must be stated in the output. Minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, independent filtering at alpha 0.05, BH adjustment, apeglm shrinkage for ranking and plotting, unshrunken LFC and lfcSE retained. (T2S1) preranked GSEA with gseapy on the full ranked list of tested genes, ranked by the Wald statistic (the disputed ranking-metric choice is settled here in favour of the Wald stat: it is signed and scaled by its standard error, which matters when one shallow library inflates the uncertainty of low-count genes), against the human MSigDB Hallmark collection first, then GO BP and human WikiPathways as follow-up collections, each reported with its release and never merged. (T1S3) a consolidated report tying the gene table, the fit diagnostics, the leading-edge genes of each significant hallmark set, and the reproducibility record together, with the depth caveat for sample_01 and the missing-length-offset caveat stated explicitly.

With 6 vs 6 the design is adequately but not generously powered; results are hypothesis-generating for pathway-level claims, and the report must say so rather than assert mechanism.

State plainly, not in a footnote: (1) sample_01's library size is about 4x below the median, what the QC showed about it, and whether it was kept; (2) the Salmon gene-level counts carry no established length correction and no length offset was applied, so an isoform-usage shift can present as differential expression; (3) enrichment results are method-dependent and are hypotheses for follow-up; (4) 6 vs 6 is a modest sample size — do not present pathway-level findings as established mechanism. Close with a reproducibility record: package versions, the permutation seed, the gene-set collection releases, and the session information. Also produce a volcano plot on the shrunken LFC and a heatmap of the top differentially expressed genes on the VST matrix.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
